narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 63% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That does not mean default is certain, but it is above the bank’s acceptable risk level, so the application did not proceed.

The strongest factor was your checking account status: being overdrawn (below zero) is much less common among approved applicants than having no overdraft or a positive balance, and this pushed the prediction toward bad credit. The second most important factor was the amount requested. At 1,659 DM, well below the approved average of about 3,020 DM, this actually worked in your favour and reduced the perceived risk. The third factor was the requested repayment period of 24 months, longer than the approved average of about 19 months, which pushed the prediction back toward bad credit.

To improve your chances, focus on bringing your checking account out of overdraft and keeping it in good standing. Ask the bank whether a shorter repayment period would be possible, since the requested amount itself was already favourable. You could also ask about adding a guarantor or co-applicant, and seek credit counselling if past payment difficulties are still affecting your record.
